title: Personal Sender Account Tenure and the Bank Deposit Shortfall Delivery Rate
content:
The make-good delivery rate on a Bank Deposit shortfall delivery carries a tenure rate bonus, in percentage points of the booking-day reference, that follows how long the customer's Personal Sender Account has been open.

## Clause

Tenure is counted in whole calendar months from the Personal Sender Account's opening date to the handling date, never from the date its current level took effect. A tenure of at least 60 months earns the long-tenure bonus of 0.30 percentage points; at least 24 months but less than 60 months earns the mid-tenure bonus of 0.15 percentage points; a shorter tenure earns no tenure rate bonus.

| Whole calendar months since the account was opened | Tenure rate bonus |
|---|---|
| 60 or more | 0.30 percentage points |
| 24 to 59 | 0.15 percentage points |
| fewer than 24 | none |

## Questions the rule answers

**The account was opened 61 months ago but moved up to its current level last year. Which date counts?** The opening date: 61 months, so 0.30.

**Exactly 60 whole months?** 0.30; at least 60.

**59 whole months?** 0.15.

**24 whole months?** 0.15; at least 24.

**23 whole months?** No tenure rate bonus.

*Hypothetical month count:* an account opened on 20 March 2024, handled on 19 March 2026, has 23 whole calendar months (the 24th month completes on 20 March 2026).
